declarations.docstring: Evaluating the indicated negative power at a general linear matrix yields the corresponding power of the inverse determinant.
A natural-number-indexed family of submodules in the localization away from the auxiliary matrix polynomial.
The degree filtration on the localization is monotone in its natural-number index.
The zeroth filtered submodule is the range of the canonical linear map from the matrix-entry polynomial ring.
For positive degree, the quotient of one filtration level by the preceding level is linearly equivalent to the matrix-polynomial quotient by the displayed submodule.
The linear map from a filtered localization submodule to the quotient of the matrix-entry polynomial ring by the displayed submodule.
An auxiliary statement whose displayed formal type contains an elided term.
An auxiliary statement whose displayed formal type contains an elided term.
The linear map from each filtration level to the polynomial quotient is surjective.
The supremum of all levels of the localization degree filtration is the full localization.
At positive degree, the kernel of the map to the polynomial quotient is the preceding filtration level pulled back to the current subtype.
Every level of the localization degree filtration is stable under the displayed general linear group action.
Acting on a degree-indexed polynomial embedding produces the embedded transformed polynomial scaled by the matching inverse determinant power.
A matrix-entry polynomial belongs to the displayed submodule exactly when it is divisible by the auxiliary matrix polynomial.
A localized element belongs to filtration level `r` exactly when its denominator order is at most `r`.
Membership in filtration level `r` is equivalent to having a polynomial-numerator presentation with inverse exponent `r`.
The matrix-entry polynomial ring is linearly equivalent to each filtered localization subtype.
The underlying localized element of the filtration equivalence is the degree-indexed polynomial embedding.
The linear map sending a matrix-entry polynomial into the localization at a specified inverse-power degree.
The degree-`r` embedding sends a polynomial to its canonical localized image multiplied by the `r`-th power of the distinguished inverse.
The degree-indexed linear embedding of matrix-entry polynomials into the localization is injective.
At positive degree, an embedded polynomial lies in the preceding filtration level exactly when the auxiliary polynomial divides it.
The degree-zero polynomial embedding is the linear map underlying the canonical algebra homomorphism into the localization.
